name: list
description: Rich list rows — leading avatar, icon tile or thumbnail; title, subtitle and right-aligned meta; trailing content — with grouped sections under sticky headers, dividers, inset cards and three densities. Plain list semantics by default; data-selection='single|multi' makes it a WAI-ARIA listbox with roving focus, type-ahead, Shift range selection and Ctrl/Cmd+A; data-reorderable adds pointer dragging by a handle with a drop indicator and keyboard reordering, every move announced and emitted as faqir:reorder.

toolbar.description: Row above the items — it stays put while a capped list scrolls its rows — for a count and the actions that apply to the selection ('3 selected · Archive'). It is the answer to per-row actions in a selectable list: an option may not contain controls, so act on getSelected() from here.

items.description: The list. A <ul> or <ol> holding items, or sections. Selectable: the controller gives it role='listbox' and aria-multiselectable; give it an aria-label (or aria-labelledby). Inside a section, the inner [data-part='items'] holds that section's items and gets role='none'. It is the scroller: a list capped with --list-max-height scrolls here, under its sticky section headers.

section.description: A group of items under a header. Selectable: role='group' with aria-labelledby pointing at its header (the controller wires both, giving the header an id when it has none).

header.description: The section's sticky header — it sticks inside its own section, so the next one pushes it off. In a plain list make it a heading (<h3>) so it is in the outline; in a selectable list it must be a role='presentation' <span> (a listbox may hold only groups and options), named to its group by aria-labelledby.

item.description: One row, a direct child of [data-part='items']. Selectable: role='option' with aria-selected and a roving tabindex. aria-disabled='true' dims it and takes it out of focus and selection. data-value is its identity; data-accent colours its icon tile.

handle.description: Drag grip, shown only on a data-reorderable list. In a plain list a <button> (labelled 'Reorder {title}' when it has no label) that also offers a keyboard grab mode; in a selectable list a decorative aria-hidden <span> — the focused option moves with Alt+Up/Down instead.

leading.description: Leading media: an avatar primitive, an icon primitive (drawn as an accent tile) or an thumbnail. Decorative when the title names the row.

content.description: Stacks the title over the subtitle and takes the free width.

title.description: The row's name, truncated to one line; used for type-ahead and reorder announcements. In a plain list a link or button inside it stretches over the whole row.

subtitle.description: Second line (a preview, an address, a status). Its presence puts the meta on the title line and lets a count or badge drop beneath it.

meta.description: Right-aligned short text — a time, a value, a count. Beside the trailing part on a one-line row; on the title line of a two-line row (centred when a control sits beside it). Takes the accent while the row shows a count.

trailing.description: Trailing content: a count, a badge, a chevron, a switch — and, in a plain list only, action buttons (they sit above a stretched title link). In a selectable list keep it non-interactive. On a two-line row a count or badge here drops beneath the meta.

count.description: Inside trailing: an unread count drawn as a solid accent pill. While it is shown the row's meta turns accent too, and on a two-line row it drops beneath the meta. Put the number in an aria-hidden span and a visually hidden ' unread' beside it, so the option's name says what the number is.

empty.description: Shown when the list has no items (data-state='empty', which the controller sets and clears as items come and go).

live.description: Visually hidden role='status' region the controller announces reorders in. Created on first use when absent; author one to control its placement.

style.description: plain = rows only; divided = a hairline between rows, inset past the leading media; inset = each section (or the whole list) as a rounded card on a subtle ground, iOS settings style.

size.description: Row density: padding, gaps and title size.

empty.description: No items: the items container is hidden and [data-part='empty'] shows.

dragging.description: A reorder is in progress: on the root, and on the item being moved — by the pointer (it follows it via --list-drag-y) or from the keyboard (held in grab mode).

drop-before.description: Pointer drag indicator: the dragged item will land before this one.

drop-after.description: Pointer drag indicator: the dragged item will land after this one (the last row).

selected.description: Selectable lists only: aria-selected='true' on each selected option. The DOM is the source of truth — a binding may write it and getSelected() reads it back.

disabled.description: aria-disabled='true': dimmed, skipped by focus, type-ahead and range selection, never selected.

methods.name: move
methods.description: Move an item to `index` among its siblings; returns its new index.

selection.description: none = a plain list (rows may hold links and buttons); single = a single-select listbox; multi = a multi-select listbox with a check mark per option.

reorderable.description: Shows the handles and turns on pointer and keyboard reordering. Moves stay within the item's own items container (its section).

value.description: On an item: its identity in faqir:select / faqir:reorder details and getSelected(). Falls back to the id, then the title text.

--list-max-height.description: Cap the list's height (custom property): the items container then scrolls under its sticky section headers while the toolbar stays put.

--list-bg.description: The list's ground, which the sticky section headers are filled from (custom property). Match it to the surface the list sits on.

--list-selected.description: Fill of a selected option (custom property).

required_attrs: an accessible name on the top-level items container (aria-label or aria-labelledby)
role="listbox" on items when data-selection is single or multi
role="option" and aria-selected on each item when selectable
role="group" with aria-labelledby on each section when selectable

keyboard.ArrowDown / ArrowUp: selectable: move focus to the next / previous enabled option (no wrap)
keyboard.Home / End: selectable: move focus to the first / last enabled option
keyboard.Space / Enter: single: select the focused option; multi: toggle it
keyboard.Shift + ArrowDown / ArrowUp: multi: move focus and extend the selection from the anchor
keyboard.Shift + Home / End: multi: extend the selection to the first / last option
keyboard.Shift + Space: multi: select every option from the anchor to the focused one
keyboard.Ctrl/Cmd + A: multi: select every enabled option, or clear them all when all are selected
keyboard.Printable characters: selectable: type-ahead to the next option whose title starts with the typed text (500ms buffer)
keyboard.Alt + ArrowUp / ArrowDown: reorderable: move the focused option (selectable) or the focused handle's row (plain) one place, announced
keyboard.Space / Enter on a handle: plain + reorderable: grab the row; then ArrowUp / ArrowDown move it, Space / Enter drop it, Escape cancels and restores it, and moving focus away drops it

pointer.Shift + click: multi: select the range from the anchor
pointer.drag a handle: reorderable: the row follows the pointer, an accent rule marks where it will land, release to drop

notes: Selectable lists never put controls inside an option — role='option' is a single control, so a nested button is unreachable to assistive tech and an axe nested-interactive failure. Per-row actions belong in a plain list (data-selection absent), where rows are ordinary list items; actions on a selection belong in [data-part='toolbar'] (or anywhere outside the listbox), driven by getSelected() and faqir:select.
Focus is a roving tabindex on the options themselves (one tab stop for the list); aria-selected, not focus, is the selection.
Every reorder is announced in a polite status region as 'Moved {title} to position {n} of {total}', and grab mode announces its instructions when it starts.
Handles are pointer affordances in a selectable list (aria-hidden spans) because an option may not contain a button; there the keyboard path is Alt+ArrowUp/Down on the option itself.

Sticky section headers sit on a translucent fill over a backdrop blur so they stay legible over the rows scrolling beneath them; the multi-select tick is generated content with empty alt text, so only aria-selected is announced.

faqir:select.description: After any selection change by click, keyboard or select()/toggle()/selectAll()/clear(): item/value are the option acted on (null for clear), items/values the whole selection in DOM order.

faqir:reorder.description: After a row moves, by drag, keyboard or move(): from/to are indices among its siblings, values the new order. The DOM node has already moved; mirror it into your data (a keyed l-for then agrees).
